newsitem.title: USA: Mesa Air sees load factor steady as capacity added.
newsitem.headline: Mesa Air sees load factor steady as capacity added.

text.p: Mesa Air Group Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Larry Risley said on Tuesday he expects load factor levels to hold steady as the carrier adds capacity during fiscal 1997.

"We feel the load factors are going to stabilize and maintain a fairly steady balance with any increase in capacity we might be putting in," Risley said in a telephone interview from company headquarters in Farmington, New Mexico. "Most of our capacity increase is going to take place in the third and fourth quarter of this coming year."
Risley said he expects Mesa's load factor to be between 55 percent and 56 percent during the first quarter of fiscal year 1997, ending December 30.

He also said he was comfortable with the First Call analysts' consensus projection that Mesa would post earnings per share of 14 cents in the first quarter and $1.04 for fiscal 1997. "There's nothing that gives us any level of concern in being able to achieve those numbers."
He said the addition of three, 37-passenger turbo props to Mesa's existing fleet in December 1996 would accommodate extra ski-season demand.
The planned launch next May of a new, regional jet service out of Meacham International Airport in Fort Worth, Texas, will have a significant impact on business, he said.
"There is tremendous opportunity for us for internal growth with the new regional jets we've bought," Risley said. "We feel that is going to have a material, positive impact on our earnings."
Mesa's regional jet service out of Fort Worth will start with two 50-seater aircraft and eventually grow to 10, company officials said.
A further six new 50-seaters will be based in Phoenix, Ariz. in August 1997 to replace turbo-prop aircraft currently used by Mesa affiliates Mountain West and Desert Sun.

Risley said Mesa's management will on December 6 present a proposal to its board of directors on the relocation of its corporate headquarters. An announcement on the relocation will likely be made on December 7 if the board reaches consensus, he said.
